residue.text: Retained source limitation: bright specks could be bubbles, reflections or undissolved dye. Neither their identity, bubble fraction nor the proposed return loop is established. Surface depression and speck counts are observations, not bubble identification.

Retained source limitations: common-aliquot repeatability is not concentration calibration; commanded rpm is unverified. Sampling and transfers can disturb gradients. Different cessation times create unequal quiet intervals in the feedback pair, limiting attribution of vial differences solely to additional stirring. Rapid optical changes could reflect surface shape or settling.

Source-bound omitted option: INV proposes a matched seconds-45-to-50 pause, resuming until second 65 for 60 total stirring seconds, if two trials remain. The selected six-trial schedule leaves none; this hypothesis-testing option remains pending, and pauses also alter transport and settling.

Retained source scope: replication is limited, relative time savings lack an observed preferred-procedure duration, and other liquids, vessels and continuous processes are untested. Syringe low-to-high redistribution is available but untested in this schedule; no successful outcome is inferred for it.

summary.text: Observed synthetic evidence: one 300 rpm run stopped at second 60 yielded final attenuations 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. This challenges universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm and optical stability, without proving reliable sufficiency. Fluctuating 900 rpm images lack matched final vials.

Retain rival hypotheses: agitation-generated optical disturbance may renew failed checks and prolong agitation; alternatively, actual depth gradients may cause failed checks and benefit from further mixing. A persistent optical artifact is another unresolved explanation. The return mechanism and reversed agitation-to-image arrow remain hypotheses.

Proposed six trials: two fresh fixed 300/900 rpm pairs, reversing speed order, each stirring exactly 60 seconds without optical restart; then a fresh 900 rpm timer-stop versus enabled-rule pair, capped at second 105. Sample at second 120. Fix recipe, addition location, bottle and camera; alternate sampling order and use references.

Predictions, not outcomes: greater moving-image disturbance at 900 rpm followed by prompt decline and passing vials would support an agitation-to-image effect. Both feedback trials passing, with shadow failures and shorter timer stirring, would support a costly return dependency. Timer failure with enabled success would favor useful additional mixing, without establishing this speed or rule necessary. Both failures or overlapping results leave rivals unresolved.

Log five-second images, shadow decisions, depression, specks, cessation times, stirring seconds, transfers and raw vials; report every target failure. Final-vial spread at most 4 percent determines bounded success; stable images alone cannot. Use spill tray and stop on escaped liquid. No real chemical or human benefit is established.
